12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the nine-month actual, not on a forecast: net sales of IDR 4,300.75bn against IDR 3,934.95bn a year earlier, +9.3 per cent, with the feed segment down 7.2 per cent while breeder and farm grew 35.1 per cent and dressed chicken 16.0 per cent (S4, F12, F13). The fourth quarter is set on its own seasonal shape rather than extrapolated: Q4 2025 was the strongest quarter (net profit IDR 24.2bn against a nine-month profit of IDR 5.1bn, S0), and Q4 2026 is entered a few points above the year-ago quarter, which leaves FY2026E growth just under the nine-month rate. Growth then tapers with the volume the asset base can carry without new capacity: feed output was 464,926 MT against 750,000 MT of capacity and dressed chicken 45,769 MT against 76,466 MT (S5, F21-F24), so the first years are utilisation, not new plant. No source discloses a plan to repeat a double-digit year (S4, S5).

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: The witnessed FY2025 margin is the reference: net sales IDR 5,441.5bn less cost of sales IDR 4,945.5bn is 9.12 per cent (S3, F1, F3), split by segment into feed 7.1 per cent, breeder and farm 5.6 per cent and dressed chicken and frozen foods 10.2 per cent on their total (external plus inter-segment) revenue (S3, F16-F19). The input is the margin the business earns at a given input cost; the engine then charges the agri deck's corn and soymeal moves through the two cost links, which carry only the witnessed domestic input-cost part of the move (about 1.2 points). The rest of the margin fall witnessed in the nine months of 2026 - net sales IDR 4,300.75bn less cost of sales IDR 3,992.05bn, 7.18 per cent (S4, F12, F13) - is not input cost and is carried here: feed external revenue fell 7.2 per cent while breeder and farm grew 35.1 per cent and dressed chicken 16.0 per cent, and breeder and farm is the group's lowest-margin segment at 5.6 per cent (S4, S3, F16-F19). The mix shift and the live-bird price below the producer's cost of production (S6, F31, F32) are therefore a sourced, permanent-in-the-base drift of about 0.9 points below the FY2025 at-base margin, not a haircut: the FY2026E input is 8.49 per cent against 9.39 per cent before the mix adjustment. The margin then recovers with utilisation: feed runs at 62 per cent of capacity and the doubled dressed chicken line at 60 per cent with processed-food utilisation stated at about 50 per cent (S5, F21-F24, F26), so fixed cost absorption, not a price assumption, is what lifts the at-base margin to 10.2 per cent by FY2030E and 11.1 per cent in the terminal year - the last step is the arithmetic of the template, because the agri deck escalates corn and soymeal at about 2.2 per cent a year past its last sourced point (corn 242.7 and soymeal 506.4 by FY2035E, S0) and with revenue growing at 4 per cent the at-base margin has to rise with that curve for the realised margin to stay where it is. Realised, the FY2026E margin is 7.4 per cent, matching the witnessed nine months, and the recovery tops out at about 9.3 per cent - the FY2025 actual, once mix normalises and utilisation is repaired. No unexplained margin relief, and no haircut either.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1 (corn): effective share of COGS exposed to the deck series
assumptions.basis: Fifteen per cent effective, derived in two steps. The physical base first: feed output of 464,926 MT (S5, F21) at a conventional 50 per cent corn inclusion is 232,463 MT; at the IDR 7,000 per kg the company cites for the fourth quarter of 2025 (S5, F36) that is about IDR 1.6tn, some 30 per cent of FY2025 cost of sales of IDR 4,945.5bn (S3, F3) once allowance is made for the peak price being above the year average. Second, the deck link is not the price SIPD pays: d.agri.corn is a global benchmark, and from FY2025A to FY2026E it rises 24.3 per cent while the domestic corn SIPD buys went from Rp7,000/kg in Q4 2025 (S5, F36) to Rp7,800-8,000 in November 2026 (S6, F33), +11-14 per cent. Charging the deck change at the physical share would charge the company for a move it did not pay. The effective share is therefore the physical 30 per cent scaled by the witnessed domestic move over the deck move (30% x 12.5/24.3 = 15.4%), rounded to 15 per cent. What the link now charges is the witnessed input-cost part of the margin fall; the rest of the witnessed fall is segment mix and price, which the engine has no channel for and which is carried in gross_margin (see that basis and qc_justifications). The same effective share is held for every forecast year.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1 (corn): pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Seventy-eight per cent. Feed is re-priced to farmers on a monthly list and dressed chicken carries a wholesale price, so most of a corn move passes through; the part that does not is what the farm segment absorbs when live-bird prices are set daily in a market the group does not clear (S6). The level is calibrated on the witnessed year, not chosen: corn at the domestic +11-14 per cent move (S5, F36 to S6, F33) on the 12 per cent effective share, and soymeal at the witnessed +12.3 per cent (S0 spot against FY2025A) on 6.5 per cent, charges about one percentage point of gross margin net of pass-through, which is the input-cost part of the witnessed fall from the FY2025 margin of 9.12 per cent to the 7.18 per cent of the nine months of 2026 (S3, F1, F3, S4, F12, F13). The remaining fall is segment mix, carried in gross_margin. Higher pass-through would leave even the witnessed input-cost part unexplained.

assumptions.label: Cost link 2 (soymeal): effective share of COGS exposed to the deck series
assumptions.basis: Six and a half per cent effective. Physical base: 20 per cent soybean meal inclusion on 464,926 MT of feed (S5, F21) at the IDR 10,000 per kg the market quotes for imported soybean meal in November 2026 (S6, F34) is about IDR 0.9tn, or 19 per cent of the FY2025 cost of sales (S3, F3), carried at 13 per cent because part of the meal cost sits in the inter-segment feed price already eliminated on consolidation (S3, F19). That 13 per cent is then scaled the same way as the corn link, because d.agri.soymeal rises 28.0 per cent from FY2025A to FY2026E while the rupiah meal price witnessed in November 2026 is 12.3 per cent above the FY2025A deck average (S0 spot 360.57 against 321.15): 13% x 12.3/28.0 = 5.7%, rounded up to 6.5 per cent because the rupiah link also carries the exchange rate and part of the meal is bought forward. With the corn link it charges about 1.2 percentage points of gross margin at the 78 per cent pass-through, inside the 0.4-1.3 point range the witnessed domestic moves imply. An ordered estimate, disclosed as such.

assumptions.label: Cost link 2 (soymeal): pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Seventy-eight per cent, mirroring the corn link: the same monthly feed list and the same spot protein market sit behind both, and no source supports treating the two inputs differently. Mirroring keeps the two channels from smuggling an unstated margin assumption into the base case, and it is the value that reproduces the witnessed nine-month margin alongside the corn link (S3, F1, F3, S4, F12, F13).

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The witnessed nine months, not the three-year engine default: selling expenses of IDR 219.7bn plus general and administrative expenses of IDR 140.3bn on net sales of IDR 4,300.75bn is 8.4 per cent before the biological-asset fair-value line (S4, F12), against 7.6 per cent in FY2025 (S3). The ratio eases to 7.5 per cent as revenue grows because the overhead base did not step up with the 2026 sales (selling expenses rose 10 per cent on a 9.3 per cent top line, S4), and it is held flat in real terms thereafter. No cost-cutting story is assumed.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated away from the engine default, which reads 0.31 per cent of revenue and is the direct-method artefact the data pack carries: total depreciation and amortisation in the audited segment note is IDR 98,191m for FY2025 and IDR 93,842m for FY2024 (S3, F5, F6), not the IDR 17.0bn the pack shows, on IDR 1,099bn of net property, plant and equipment (S0). That is 1.80 per cent of FY2025 revenue; the forecast holds 1.75 per cent because capex runs above the charge (IDR 182.3bn against IDR 98.2bn, S3, F5, F7), so the asset base grows and the nominal charge grows with it. EBITDA is EBIT plus this charge, so the forecast EBITDA the pack understated is rebuilt here.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: The witnessed spend, restated from the audited segment note: total capital expenditure of IDR 182.3bn in FY2025 and IDR 270.2bn in FY2024 (S3, F7, F8), of which the dressed chicken line took IDR 141.6bn as the East Java frozen-food plant was completed (S3, S5). FY2026E is far lower because the group cut spending to protect liquidity - H1 2026 capex was IDR 23.2bn against IDR 103.9bn a year earlier (S0) - and the base case then returns to a maintenance level, converging by FY2030E on the D&A charge so that the perpetuity is not charged for growth capex the business has not announced. No new plant is assumed.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The witnessed September position, not a normalisation: trade receivables of IDR 525.3bn and inventories of IDR 596.7bn against trade payables of IDR 370.1bn at 30 September 2026 (S4) is IDR 751.9bn of non-cash working capital, 13.1 per cent of the nine months' sales annualised and 12.8 per cent of our FY2026E revenue. The ratio carried is 13.1 per cent and is held flat: the FY2025 level of 9.5 per cent (S0) is the pre-shock cycle, supplier financing has been raised against payables (S4, F10) so the payable side will not extend further, and nothing in the deck's corn and soymeal curve says the input price that drives the inventory value falls back. Easing it would be an unsourced cash release in the year the balance sheet actually widened.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The 22 per cent statutory rate, not the three-year engine default of 35 per cent: FY2025's 46.7 per cent charge is distorted by non-deductible items and the nine-month 2026 result is a tax benefit on a loss (S4, F14), so neither witnessed rate is a rate the business pays on normalised profit. The forward rate used in the discount-rate build is the same 22 per cent (S0), and the group has no minority interests (S0).

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: One cost of debt for the whole model, the same number the discount rate uses: the house macro deck's long rupiah risk-free rate plus the corporate debt spread, 9.45 per cent (S0), which is the marginal rate on the facilities the group refinanced into in 2026. On the opening balance it reproduces the witnessed charge: finance costs of IDR 44.5bn in nine months (S4, F15) annualise to about IDR 59bn, and 9.45 per cent on the IDR 599.1bn of debt at 31 December 2025 (S4, F10) is IDR 56.6bn. The earlier draft used a 7.2 per cent average, which was a blend of pre-refinancing facilities and sat below the cost of debt used in the discount rate - one rate, sourced to the witnessed charge and the deck, now does both jobs.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: The witnessed nine-month ratio: finance income of IDR 2.0bn on average cash near IDR 120bn is about 2.2 per cent, below the 2.76 per cent three-year default because deposits are short and the cash balance is thin (S4, F9, S0). Carried at 2.5 per cent.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The cash the company actually raised, not the accounting change in debt: net cash generated from financing activities in the nine months to September 2026 was IDR 263.0bn (S4, p.9), against a balance-sheet increase in total debt of IDR 383.2bn from IDR 599.1bn to IDR 982.3bn (S4, F10). The difference is non-cash - lease additions under PSAK 73, exchange on dollar facilities and supplier-financing recognised in operating flows - and booking the balance-sheet delta as a cash inflow is what forced the model's FY2026E cash balance above the September actual. The FY2026E entry is therefore the witnessed financing inflow. Nothing is added after that: the base case does not assume a facility it has not announced, and the group has shown no willingness to repay with an operating cash flow that did not cover interest in nine months of 2026 (S4). From FY2027E the free cash flow is still negative at the witnessed working-capital intensity while the working capital grows with revenue, so the model draws a modest revolver - the facility the group has been rolling - to hold the cash balance near its FY2025 level rather than letting it turn negative; the draw is the arithmetic of the cash flow, not an assumed expansion facility, and it is smaller than the FY2026 refinancing.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Held at zero. The two non-operating items in the witnessed years are the biological-asset fair-value change and other income; both are already inside the SG&A ratio the forecast uses because the data pack nets the fair-value line against operating expenses (S0, S3), and double-counting them here would add an unsourced gain.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Zero: the group has no non-controlling interests on its balance sheet at 30 September 2026 and the two subsidiaries are wholly owned (S4, S5).

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero, and that is the witnessed policy rather than a cautious assumption: the 2025 annual meeting resolved to put the whole of the FY2025 profit to a general reserve and retained earnings for working capital, with no dividend declared (S4), and no dividend has been paid in the price history (S0). A payout would have to come out of a profit the nine-month result does not show (S4, F14).

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero: 1,839,102,056 shares are in issue and unchanged since the 2023 rights issue (S3, S5). Any future equity raise would be a new decision, not a base-case line.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Four per cent, the rate the covered POULTRY_FEED peers use on the same house macro deck, so the perpetuity is consistent across the industry rather than name-specific. It sits above the deck's 3.28 per cent CPI because it carries real volume - a domestic protein and feed business grows with population and per-capita income - and below the deck's 5.29 per cent real GDP, so it does not assume share gain in perpetuity (S0).

challenges.section: 1. Business description / 2. Industry overview / 5. Risks / 7. Catalysts
challenges.challenge: S7 says 242 thousand tonnes is the NATIONAL maximum SPHP feed-corn allocation (Rp678bn budget, 213.2k t distribution target, 55.5k t realised to 29 June 2026), delivered through co-operatives and associations to 5,543 registered micro, small and medium smallholders at Rp5,000-5,500/kg. The report states four times that this is SIPD's own allocation - s1 'with an allocation of 242 000 MT', s2 'Sreeya Sewu's share of it was 242 000 MT ... a genuine cost advantage', s5 as a policy risk, s7 'Sreeya Sewu's allocation of 242 thousand tonnes ... is the base to compare against' - and the bull narrative uses it as a corn-cost cap (fund record line 424). No source connects SIPD to the programme, and F37 is mis-keyed 'corn_supply_support' as though it were company-specific.
challenges.answer: Deleted SIPD from the SPHP programme in section 1, 2, 5 and 7 and re-keyed F37 as the national allocation: 242 thousand tonnes for all recipients, sold through co-operatives to registered smallholders [S7]. The programme is now described as a cap on the domestic corn price and a support to smallholder feed demand, not a company cost advantage. The bull narrative states that no filing names SIPD as a recipient and does not assume one.

challenges.challenge: The FY2026 gross-margin charge is built from the deck's FY2025A-to-FY2026E corn and soymeal change (+24.3% and +28.0%: 172.56 to 214.57 and 321.15 to 411.00) at a fitted 78% pass-through, which charges 1.9pp of gross margin. The deck's own 11-Nov-2026 spot is 175.39 and 360.57, i.e. +1.6% and +12.3% on FY2025A, and the company's domestic corn went Rp7,000/kg in Q4 2025 (F36) to Rp7,800-8,000/kg in Nov 2026 (F33), +11-14%. At those witnessed moves the same links charge roughly 0.4-1.3pp, or IDR 35-65bn of FY2026 EBITDA. The rest of the 1.94pp nine-month margin fall is segment mix - breeder revenue +35.1% at a 5.6% segment margin against feed 7.1% and dressed chicken 10.2% - which the report never bridges; and 78% pass-through is one equation fitted to two unknowns (share and pass-through), both of which the basis itself calls ordered estimates.
challenges.answer: Rebuilt both input links on the witnessed domestic series rather than the deck percentage: corn from F36 at Rp7,000 in Q4 2025 to F33 at Rp7,800-8,000 in November 2026, and imported meal at F34 [S6][S5]. link1_share is now 0.15 and link2_share 0.065 with pass-through held at 0.78. Section 3 carries a margin bridge splitting input cost from segment mix, showing dressed-chicken segment gross profit falling while feed rose [S3]. Section 4 states the deck-spot test and places a sustained lower input price in the bull, anchored on the FY2023 margin.

challenges.challenge: The auditor is described as 'a mid-tier national practice' and the opinion discounted because it is 'not the assurance a top-tier engagement would give'. In the same annual report the KAP table for this very engagement lists 'Rintis, Jumadi, Rianto & Rekan ... www.pwc.com' - it is PwC Indonesia, a Big Four member firm. Both sentences are contradicted by the source cited, and they tilt the governance assessment negative on a false fact.
challenges.answer: Corrected section 6: the auditor is KAP Rintis, Jumadi, Rianto & Rekan, PwC's Indonesian member firm and formerly Tanudiredja, Wibisana, Rintis & Rekan, with Andry Danil Atmadja as signing partner and an unqualified opinion [S5]. The mid-tier sentence is deleted and the governance assessment no longer discounts audit quality; the finding is now neutral to positive.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 states 'Weights of 50% DCF, 20% EV/EBITDA and 30% P/BV give a weighted value of Rp286.' The method weights give 185.1 (0.5 x 0 + 0.2 x 0 + 0.3 x 617.1); 286.1 is the probability-weighted scenario value (0.5 x 214.4 + 0.3 x 214.4 + 0.2 x 573.0), and the engine's own construction line reports 'method blend today 185 ... probability-weighted scenarios 286 ... target 200'. The reader cannot reproduce the target from the text, and the sentence conceals that the 33% step from 214 to 286 comes from the 20% bull weight.
challenges.answer: Section 4 and the summary now show the chain in order as val.v0 then val.tp_base then val.tp_weighted then val.tp_final, with the 50/20/30 weights, and state that the two earnings methods return zero so the blend is the book leg times its weight and the bull case alone carries the lift. The absolute numbers moved with the revised probabilities and the constitution liquidity charge, so the old 286 and 200 pair no longer describes this model.

challenges.challenge: The EV/EBITDA cross-check is described in the summary and in section 4 as applied to 'trough-year EBITDA', but fund record applies 4.684x to FY2025A EBITDA of 183.5, giving equity of -5.8 on book equity of 1,179 - within 0.7% of zero. On the trough metric (FY2026E 79.3) the leg would be -494 of equity, and at CPRO's 4.88x or CPIN's 5.14x the leg would be positive. The claim that 'two methods failing in the same direction are not independent confirmations but a joint statement that the capital structure is the dominant fact' therefore rests on a coincidence, not on agreement.
challenges.answer: Dropped the trough description. The EV/EBITDA cross-check is now stated as applied to FY2025A restated EBITDA of 183.5 [S3], disclosed as producing a small negative equity value unfloored, and the DCF is stated to be negative by more than its own enterprise value. The engine valuation table floors both methods at zero, so the distance below zero is given in prose rather than in the table.

challenges.challenge: P/BV determines 100% of the effective valuation, because the other 70% of the weight returns exactly zero. The industry config sets multiple_source: blend; the model uses peer_median alone, which halves the leg (own_history P/BV mean 1.932x, n=4, against the 0.962x peer median). Section 4 justifies dropping own history with 'the own history - 0.9x at the current price', which is the spot multiple (0.936x), not the own-history figure. On own history the leg is Rp948 per share and the target is roughly Rp300, not Rp200.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now discloses that the house default is the own-history multiple, that the own-history mean is roughly twice the peer median (1.93x on four observations against 0.96x), and that the override to peer median is against the company and material. The wrong 0.9x-at-current-price phrase is gone. We keep peer_median because own history prices a return on equity this business no longer earns. We hold no dated own-history series to publish beyond the pack.

challenges.challenge: The cost of equity is 15.8% and the report says it 'sits at the top of the house band'; VAL_COMPOUNDER_QUALITY pins the IDR COE/WACC band at 11-13%, so it is 2.8pp outside and the out-of-band argument is owed. The argument offered is the instrument's illiquidity ('a public float of 9.2% ... no ability to exit at a mark'), and the same illiquidity is then charged a second time as an unsourced 30% liquidity discount - 'applied separately so that the two are not hidden in one number' is exactly the double count. Separately, the 9.45% pre-tax cost of debt is said to be 'what the company's floating-rate facilities imply [S3]', but S3 gives 59.4 on average debt of 811.6 (7.3%) and F15 gives 44.5 in nine months, 7.0% annualised, while the model's own cost_of_debt input is 7.2%.
challenges.answer: The out-of-band cost of equity is lodged against the card with the arithmetic shown: unlevered beta 0.90 at D/E 0.85 and tax 22% gives a levered beta of 1.50, so bringing COE inside 11-13% would require an unsourced beta cut, while WACC at 12.0% is inside the band. The 30% discount is sourced to the constitution ADTV band below Rp100m and is charged once on equity value, not in the discount rate. Cost of debt is a single 9.45% rate used in both the WACC and the profit and loss account [S3][S4].

challenges.challenge: The sensitivity grid returns all zeros and the report calls that 'the floor, not an error'. An exhibit that cannot vary is not an exhibit: with DCF equity at -Rp283 per share unfloored (EV 344.8 against net debt 865.5), no WACC +/-1pp or g +/-1pp inside the grid reaches zero, and the second grid is flat at 214.4 for gross margin -2pp, -1pp and 0, so it shows no downside response either. The card also requires reinvestment rate and ROIIC, a fade year, and the multiple-survival test - the implied exit EV/EBITDA is 579.4/254.3 = 2.28x against a 4.68x entry multiple - none of which appears.
challenges.answer: Added the reinvestment and owner-earnings bridge, the incremental-return discussion, the fade test and the implied exit multiple against the entry multiple in section 4. The sensitivity grid is generated from the industry template and its DCF axis is pinned at zero by the floor; the text now explains the boundary and names the book multiple and the liquidity charge as the axes that actually move the target, with the unfloored DCF disclosed in prose.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E puts IDR 40.3bn of the year's IDR 79.3bn EBITDA - 51% - into the fourth quarter, which is 9.3x the nine-month quarterly run-rate of IDR 4.3bn (nine-month EBITDA is 38.9bn on the model's own convention, D&A 81.1 per S4 note). The basis cites 'Q4 2025 was the strongest quarter (net profit IDR 24.2bn against a nine-month profit of IDR 5.1bn, S0)', but that quarter contains IDR 47.3bn of the FY2025 biological-asset fair-value gain (FY 49.109 less 9M 1.790); ex-fair-value the Q4 2025 quarter was about 4x its nine-month run-rate, so the model needs a spike twice as large as last year's, in a quarter with no data. The engine's calibration flag (FY2026E margin 1.35% against FY2025A 3.37%, gap -2.02pp) is left unanswered.
challenges.answer: Rebuttal on the mechanism, acceptance on the disclosure. The fourth-quarter concentration is arithmetic once nine-month EBIT is negative, and the implied fourth-quarter operating result is below Q4 2025 ex-fair-value. Nine-month depreciation of 81.1 [S4 note 28] already ran close to FY2025's 98.2 [S3], so the add-back is not back-loaded. Section 3 now sets this out and the calibration gap is justified in qc_justifications against the deck's year-average versus witnessed prices.

challenges.challenge: The FY2026E balance sheet does not reconcile to the 30 September 2026 actuals the report rebases on. Net debt FY2026E is 715.9 against 865.5 actual: the model books the whole nine-month debt inflow (383.2) into FY2026E and also runs a full year of FCFF from the December 2025 base, which forces Q4 2026 to generate about 150bn of cash. NWC FY2026E is 704.6 against 751.9 actual (receivables 525.3 + inventories 596.7 - payables 370.1, the report's own figures), yet the report says the cycle is stretching and carries 12.0% against the witnessed 13.1%. Interest is charged on opening debt, so FY2026E finance costs of 43.1 are below the 44.5 already incurred in nine months (F15).
challenges.answer: Cost of debt is now one 9.45% rate reproducing the witnessed annualised charge on opening debt, and NWC is held at the witnessed 13.1% [S4]. Net borrowing is cut to the witnessed nine-month financing inflow, so FY2026E net debt is 800.6 against the 865.5 September actual. Section 3 discloses that the template runs a full year from the December base and cannot be split quarterly, and that the valuation deducts the September actual rather than the forecast.

challenges.challenge: The report dismisses the price gap in one line as 'the controlling shareholder's option value or a control premium a minority holder cannot access' but never tests the exit a minority holder actually has. PT Great Giant Pineapple holds 90.78% and must lift public float from 9.22% to 15% - 106.3m shares, Rp67bn at Rp630, against ADTV of Rp51m/day - so a tender offer, squeeze-out or block placement at a premium is the cheapest route for the controller, and IDX tender rules set a floor price. The entire free float is worth about Rp107bn, so the controller can support or reprice the stock; that is why a 0.9x-book price may be option value rather than a valuation error.
challenges.answer: Section 6 now values the free float against the parent's balance sheet, cites the ADTV, sets out the tender or squeeze-out as the only premium exit and the block placement as supply in the bear, and states that no borrow is available so a SELL speaks to an owner rather than to a short seller [S0][S8]. The tender is folded into the bull rather than a fourth scenario because the engine scenario set is three. We assert no exchange minimum-price rule because we hold no archived rule text.

challenges.challenge: There is no asset-value floor anywhere. DCF EV of 344.8 is 0.31x FY2025A net PP&E of 1,099 and 0.17x invested capital of 2,044 (equity 1,179 plus net debt 865), so the DCF implies the plants are worth less than a third of their book cost while the P/BV leg assumes 0.96x - the two are inconsistent and only the book leg is used for 30% of the weight. The industry archetypes include washout_rebound, yet the bull case only adds 3pp of revenue growth and 2pp of gross margin and never tests a reversion to the FY2023 realised gross margin of 9.4% on the deck's terminal inputs, which is the obvious recovery case; at GM +2pp the DCF already unfloors (bull v0 494.7 against base 185.1).
challenges.answer: Added an asset-value cross-check comparing the DCF enterprise value with net property, plant and equipment of 1,099 and with book equity plus September net debt [S3][S4], and a washout test whose gross margin is the FY2023 realised 9.4% and whose EBIT margin is the FY2023 1.8%, with the entry EV/EBITDA and P/BV the current price implies under them.

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality screen never mentions the IDR 49.1bn biological-asset fair-value gain in FY2025 (S3: 'Perubahan atas nilai wajar aset biologis 49,109 ... (1,073)'), which is 26.8% of the 183.5 restated EBITDA the whole report leans on and 58% of the 85.3 EBIT, with a further +9.2bn in 9M2026. Section 3 presents 'operating expense was 410.7' without saying that is net of the gain (gross selling plus G&A 459.8, EBIT ex-fair-value 36.2), and the forecast silently relies on the same netting because the 7.9% opex ratio is net of a fair-value credit. Relatedly, the report says improving EBITDA margins were 'partly a declining depreciation rate on an ageing asset base', but D&A ROSE from 93.8 to 98.2 (1.75% to 1.80% of revenue, F5/F6) - the margin improvement is the fair-value swing, not depreciation.
challenges.answer: Added a fair-value line to the earnings-quality screen with F40 at 49.109 for FY2025 and F41 at 9.218 for nine months 2026 [S3][S4], the effect on the multiple on clean EBITDA, and the provision risk in a falling live-bird market. Deleted the declining-depreciation claim and replaced it with capex running above the charge in both years.

challenges.challenge: The 15% free-float minimum and the '31 March 2029' compliance deadline are cited to [S8] and to '[registry]'. S8 (7 February 2026) contains no '2029', says the rule raise was 'ditargetkan rampung pada Maret 2026' (targeted for completion in March 2026) and uses 'akan ditingkatkan' (will be raised), and '[registry]' is not a source at all - fund record has S0 and S2-S8 only. The report also states in section 3, on the company's own boilerplate, that the shares 'remained in full compliance with the prevailing listing requirements' while section 6 says the float is below the exchange minimum.
challenges.answer: Removed the 31 March 2029 date and the [registry] citation everywhere. The float paragraph cites S8 only for the 15% minimum, says the phased timetable is the exchange's and puts no date on it. Section 3 now reconciles the annual report's compliance boilerplate with the forward shortfall by noting the higher minimum is a new rule with phased implementation, so compliance with the rules in force and a shortfall against the new level can both be true.

challenges.challenge: No peer operating metric appears anywhere. 'Well below the scale of the largest integrators' and 'a sub-scale mill pays more for its raw material' cite nothing, although house coverage of CPIN (BUY), JPFA (BUY), AYAM (SELL) and WMPP (SELL) is available. CPIN's 9M2026 - revenue +18.9%, net profit +54% (11-Nov-2026 news) - is the single best test of whether SIPD's loss is a sector trough or company-specific, and its absence lets the bull case attribute to the cycle a problem that may be segment mix and scale.
challenges.answer: Added the peer test: CPIN nine months 2026 revenue of 60.20tn and net profit 5.18tn at an 11.33% operating margin, JPFA 3.23tn at 9.50%, against SIPD's 59.2bn loss [S9][S4], with house ratings named. Section 2 and 5 use it to show the loss is company-specific on mix and scale, and the bull probability is cut to 15% with that reason stated.

missing_bull_case.note: No take-private/squeeze-out or block-placement scenario for a 90.78% controller facing a float top-up of 106.3m shares (Rp67bn) on Rp51m/day ADTV; no replacement-cost floor even though DCF EV 344.8 is 0.31x net PP&E 1,099 and 0.17x invested capital 2,044; the bull at 573 is below the 630 price, so no scenario justifies the market and the control premium is named but never modelled.

missing_bear_case.note: The IDR 49.1bn biological-asset fair-value gain inside FY2025 EBITDA (26.8% of the 183.5 restated figure, 58% of the 85.3 EBIT) is absent from the earnings-quality screen, and 9M2026 carries a further +9.2bn; on clean EBITDA the market pays 12.3x not 9.0x. CPIN's 9M2026 net profit +54% is not used, though it shows the loss is company-specific rather than a sector trough.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E puts 51% of the year's EBITDA (IDR 40.3bn of 79.3) into Q4, 9.3x the nine-month quarterly run-rate, on a precedent (Q4 2025 net profit 24.2 vs 5.1) that is a 47.3bn fair-value gain; the cost links charge the deck's +24%/+28% input move when the deck's own 11-Nov spot is +1.6%/+12.3%; FY2026E interest (43.1) is below the 44.5 already booked in nine months.

evidence_and_citations.note: FATAL: the 242,000 MT SPHP feed-corn allocation is the national maximum (S7: Rp678bn budget, 213.2k t target, 55.5k t realised, 5,543 smallholders via co-operatives), yet is asserted four times as SIPD's own allocation and used in the bull case. Also: the auditor is called mid-tier though S5 lists www.pwc.com; '[registry]' is cited but is not a source; the 31-Mar-2029 float date is not in S8.

valuation_method_fit.note: 70% of the method weight contributes exactly zero, so 100% of the value is P/BV at 0.962x on Sep-2026 book, then rolled at a 15.8% COE although the model's own book falls to 1,128.8 by FY2027E; no implied exit multiple (DCF implies 2.28x EV/EBITDA vs 4.68x entry), no ROIIC, no owner-earnings bridge; the 30% liquidity discount is unsourced and the multiple_source config default (blend) was overridden to peer median.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose over-reads its own arithmetic: 'two methods failing in the same direction' is a coincidence (EV/EBITDA equity -5.8 on 1,179 book), the blend is reported as 286 when it is 185, and the bull narrative promises feed volume returning to 750,000 MT from 464,926 MT although the shock only adds 3pp of revenue growth.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The deck is read correctly for FY2026E (nine-month average, not a stale forecast) but the report never says the FY2027E corn and soymeal at 214.57 and 411.00 sit 22% and 14% ABOVE the deck's 11-Nov-2026 spot of 175.39 and 360.57, or that the margin path depends on that forecast; a CME percentage is applied to a domestic cost share although domestic corn is Rp7,800/kg (US$434/t) against the deck's US$214.57/t. No peer operating metric appears anywhere despite in-house CPIN, JPFA, AYAM and WMPP coverage.

conservatism_audit.note: P/BV own-history mean is 1.932x (n=4) against the 0.962x peer median actually used; the rejection cites '0.9x at the current price', which is the spot multiple, not the history. The 30% liquidity discount is charged on top of a COE whose stated rationale is the same illiquidity. No assumption is set below the last actual except the deck-sourced margin, which is disclosed and credited.

calibration.note: The engine's calibration flag (FY2026E EBITDA margin 1.35% vs FY2025A 3.37%, gap -2.02pp) is a WARN left unaddressed in qc_justifications and unexplained in the report; it is caused by the Q4 2026 recovery, which carries more than half the year's EBITDA. FY2025A itself reconciles (revenue, COGS, D&A and EBIT all tie to S3), so the restatement is sound.

signoff.notes: APPROVED. Sector reason: the two scale integrators with filed 9M-2026 profits are the BUYs (CPIN, JPFA); SIPD is a sub-scale, EBIT-loss-making feed/breeder at about 0.98x book with 90.78% control and a 9.22% float, so the SELL is coherent. Q1 is not a sign-off blocker: the engine arithmetic is self-consistent (bear and base are both 214.43; weighted 270 = 0.85 x 214.43 + 0.15 x 582; less the 30% liquidity charge = 189) and the base alone is -66% against the 630 price, so the defect biases the target UP, against the SELL. The reverse DCF cannot bracket the price at any growth rate, which is the finding rather than a failure: the gap is a margin gap, not a growth gap.
